repo.name: vscode (fork: vosbek/vscode-fence-test)
repo.summary: Visual Studio Code: a layered TypeScript codebase (base, platform, editor, workbench) built for Electron, the web and a remote server, with built-in extensions in the extension host. This map covers the whole repository at layer level and the area of one change in detail: CSS color parsing and its callers.

layers.name: Build, tests and lint rules
layers.description: The gulp and Node build, the test runners and the repository's own ESLint plugin that enforces the layering below. Tools may read any layer; product code never imports them.

layers.name: Entry points
layers.description: Processes that start VS Code: the Electron main process and CLI (src/vs/code), the remote server (src/vs/server), and the Agents window (src/vs/sessions), which may use the workbench but not the other way round.

layers.name: Workbench
layers.description: The application shell, services and every feature (contrib), plus the extension host API. May import editor, platform and base.

layers.name: Editor
layers.description: The Monaco text editor: model, view, DOM and GPU renderers, editor contributions. May import platform and base.

layers.name: Platform
layers.description: Services with dependency injection: theme, windows, files, configuration, storage. May import base only.

layers.name: Base
layers.description: General utilities with no VS Code concepts: data structures, strings, colors, DOM helpers. Imports nothing above it.

layers.name: Outside src/vs
layers.description: Built-in extensions run in the extension host and reach the core only through the vscode API.

components.name: Electron main and CLI (src/vs/code)
components.summary: Starts the Electron main process and the CLI, then opens windows through platform services.

components.name: Remote server (src/vs/server)
components.summary: The server for remote development and the web: hosts the extension host and serves the workbench.

components.name: Agents window (src/vs/sessions)
components.summary: A dedicated window for agent sessions; sits alongside the workbench and may import it, never the reverse.

components.name: Extension host API (workbench/api)
components.summary: Implements the vscode API that extensions call, on both sides of the extension host boundary.

components.name: Chat input (contrib/chat/browser/widget/input)
components.summary: The Copilot chat box: the input editor, attachments, pickers and the execute toolbar whose buttons come from the ChatExecute menu.

components.name: Chat actions (contrib/chat/browser/actions)
components.summary: Action2 classes for chat: submit, cancel, pickers, new chat. Each declares the menus it appears in and the context keys that show it.

components.name: Workbench features (workbench/contrib)
components.summary: Every feature: chat, terminal, debug, search, SCM, notebooks and about a hundred more, each a folder of contributions.

components.name: Workbench shell and services
components.summary: Layout, parts, editors, the workbench's own services and the main entry files that load every contribution.

components.name: Editor GPU renderer (editor/browser/gpu)
components.summary: Draws editor text with WebGPU. Decides per line whether it can render a decoration's CSS; anything it cannot is meant to fall back to the DOM renderer.

components.name: Editor (Monaco)
components.summary: The text model, view model, DOM view, standalone Monaco build and editor contributions.

components.name: Theme service (platform/theme)
components.summary: Color registry and theme service: every themable color is registered here and resolved to a Color.

components.name: Windows (platform/windows)
components.summary: Creates and manages Electron windows in the main process, including title bar overlay colors.

components.name: Platform services
components.summary: About 100 services (files, configuration, storage, instantiation, log, agent host) shared by every process.

components.name: Color (base/common/color.ts)
components.summary: RGBA, HSLA, HSVA and Color, plus Color.Format.CSS: format and parse CSS color strings. 160 files import it.

evidence.expect: export function parse(css: string): Color | null

components.name: Base utilities
components.summary: Lifecycle and disposables, events, async, strings, arrays, DOM helpers, the UI widgets in base/browser/ui.

components.name: Software factory tooling (.cartographer, .fence, verification)
components.summary: The codebase map and its guard rules, the fence and its configuration, and the TLA+ model of the gardener. People own the rules and the fence configuration (CODEOWNERS).

components.name: Component fixtures (UI rendered in a browser)
components.summary: Renders real workbench components with mocked services in the component explorer, for screenshots and Playwright checks. The chat input fixture adds its own toolbar items.

components.name: Repository lint rules (.eslint-plugin-local)
components.summary: VS Code's own ESLint rules. code-layering and code-import-patterns already encode the layering this map shows; they are configured as warnings, and build/eslint.ts fails on any warning or error.

components.name: Build (build/)
components.summary: gulp and Node scripts: compile, package, hygiene, the layers checker and the ESLint wrapper.

components.name: Test runners (test/, scripts/)
components.summary: Unit test runners for Electron, Node and browsers, integration and smoke tests.

components.name: Built-in extensions (extensions/)
components.summary: Language support, Git, Copilot and others; each runs in the extension host and uses only the vscode API.

edges.label: dimColor: parse a title bar color, return it unchanged when parse gives null
canRender: Color.Format.CSS.parse(value) !== null decides GPU or DOM

flows.name: A decoration's CSS color: GPU renderer or DOM fallback
flows.trigger: An extension or feature adds an inline decoration whose CSS class sets color or text-decoration-color
flows.summary: The GPU renderer asks canRender for every style rule of the decoration. A color it cannot parse should make canRender return false so the line falls back to the DOM renderer; the render strategies then parse the same value again and treat null as a bug.

steps.action: canRender reads each style rule of the decoration's class.
Color.Format.CSS.parse(value): null means not supported, so the DOM renders the line.
For rgb( and rgba( that its pattern does not match, parse throws instead of returning null, so canRender throws.

evidence.expect: throw new Error('Invalid color format ' + css);

steps.action: The render strategies parse the value again; a null here is reported as a bug (the TODO says the check belongs in canRender).

evidence.expect: throw new BugIndicatingError('Invalid color format ' + value);

flows.name: A chat input button: menu contribution to toolbar
flows.trigger: The chat input renders, or a context key it depends on changes (input has text, a request starts)
flows.summary: Buttons beside Send are not built by the chat input. An Action2 declares MenuId.ChatExecute with a when clause; the input's execute toolbar shows every item whose clause holds and runs the action with the widget as context.

steps.action: ChatSubmitAction declares the ChatExecute menu, order 4, shown when no request is active.
The input part builds its execute toolbar from the menu passed in options.
The input keeps chatInputHasText current, which when clauses can test.
The fixture adds the same menu items itself, so a new button needs a fixture line to be seen.

decisions.title: Code depends downward: base, platform, editor, workbench
decisions.context: Four million lines shared by the desktop app, the web build, the server and the standalone Monaco editor.
decisions.decision: Each layer imports only the layers below it, and each environment (common, browser, node, electron-*) only the ones it may run in.
decisions.consequences: Enforced by the repository's own lint rules code-import-patterns and code-layering (build/eslint.ts fails on any warning) and by npm run valid-layers-check. The fence runs the same lint rules on the files a change touches.

decisions.title: Color.Format.CSS.parse returns null for what it cannot read
decisions.context: Callers ask whether a CSS color is usable and fall back when it is not.
decisions.decision: The signature is Color | null and the callers in the GPU renderer and the window code test for null.
decisions.consequences: A throw for malformed rgb()/rgba() breaks both callers' fallback; this is the change in the demo pull request.

evidence.expect: export function parse(css: string): Color | null

risks.title: CSS color parse throws where callers expect null
risks.detail: rgb(255 0 0), rgba(0, 0, 0, .5) and rgb( 1, 2, 3 ) are valid CSS but do not match the parser's patterns, so parse throws. canRender in the GPU renderer would throw instead of falling back to the DOM.

evidence.expect: throw new Error('Invalid color format ' + css);
